categories.name: Linkability
categories.description: Ability to associate two or more items of interest (records, sessions, identifiers) with the same data subject without knowing identity. Risk: cross-system correlation, fingerprinting, profile aggregation.

categories.name: Identifiability
categories.description: Ability to identify a data subject within an anonymous or pseudonymous dataset. Risk: re-identification via quasi-identifiers, auxiliary data joins, model inversion.

categories.name: Non-repudiation
categories.description: Inability of a data subject to deny having performed an action, where deniability is required (e.g., whistleblowing, consent revocation). Risk: excessive logging, undeniable signatures.

categories.name: Detectability
categories.description: Ability to distinguish whether an item of interest exists, even without knowing its content. Risk: presence/absence side-channels, encrypted-flag leakage, search-pattern disclosure.

categories.name: Disclosure of Information
categories.description: Unauthorized exposure of personal data to parties beyond intended scope. Risk: PII leakage in logs, errors, third-party transfers, training corpora, embeddings.

categories.name: Unawareness and Unintervenability
categories.description: Data subjects cannot understand, access, or intervene in processing of their data. Risk: opaque consent, no access/erasure flow, no opt-out for profiling/automated decisions.

categories.name: Non-compliance
categories.description: Processing violates regulatory, contractual, or policy obligations (GDPR, HIPAA, CCPA, sector-specific rules). Risk: missing legal basis, cross-border transfer without safeguards, retention overreach.
